title: Precision tuning workflow for customer FP8/INT8 quantization exemption
creator: Sasha Kim
description: Customer request: bespoke calibration and temporary quantization exemption for a proprietary LLM used in regulated recommendations. The customer reports a >1.5% accuracy regression when we apply the default FP8 profile. They need a validated, reproducible tuning run (FP8 and fallback INT8) and a documented roll-forward/rollback plan so they can continue in production while accuracy concerns are triaged.
acceptance_criteria: Produce independent calibration runs for FP8 and INT8 with a shared seed and identical preprocessing
Validated accuracy delta (top-1 on customer eval set) <= 0.5% absolute vs baseline float16 FP32 baseline for approved profile, or documented trade-off if not achievable
Latency and p99 token latency increase <= 15% relative to baseline when serving with the approved profile
Deliver a reproducible artifact: calibration profile JSON, calibration logs, evaluation notebook, and an automated rollback script
Customer approval recorded in support thread and sign-off on the applied exemption window
runbook_steps: 1) Kick off scoped calibration job in isolated ephemeral cluster (namespace: cust-11802-calib). Use image redwood/quant-calib:2025-02. Ensure KMS access scoped to customer key (request IAM token from security team if missing).
2) Snapshot model weights (s3://cust-archival/11802/model-20250212) and mount read-only into calibration job. Do not alter production artifact.
3) Use calibration dataset provided by customer (5000 labeled examples). Sanity check: class distribution, tokenization parity, and seeding (seed=20250212).
4) Run baseline eval on float16 with same preprocessing and random seed. Persist baseline metrics and traces.
5) Run FP8 calibration profile generator (quant-calib --mode=fp8 --per-channel --clip=1.2) and persist generated profile to artifacts/11802/fp8-profile.json
6) Run INT8 calibration (quant-calib --mode=int8 --symmetric --per-tensor) as a fallback path; persist artifacts/11802/int8-profile.json

7) Evaluate both quantized variants against baseline with full eval harness (accuracy, AUC, perplexity where applicable) and token-level consistency checks; capture p99 latency using synthetic request generator with identical batch distribution

8) If FP8 meets acceptance criteria, prepare canary rollout instructions for Dedicated/Private: pin model->profile mapping in console and enable short exemption window; otherwise, document why and recommend INT8 or float16 with quantified trade-offs
9) Upload a one-click rollback script that restores previous runtime mapping and invalidates the custom profile; coordinate with on-call infra for the short approval window
10) Close loop: post run summary into support ticket and create a customer-facing report (PDF) with key graphs and artifacts links
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Sasha Kim: Triage call with support and customer (CASE-2025-2431). Customer provided a 5k eval set and allowed us a 48h exemption window to run experiments in their dedicated staging cluster.

2025-02-13 - Marco Ortega: Provisioned ephemeral staging namespace and validated access to the customer's snapshot (s3://cust-archival/11802). KMS key access required a short SR with security; SR-SEC-884 opened.

2025-02-14 - Marco Ortega: Completed baseline float16 run; baseline top-1 = 78.9% on customer eval. FP8 initial profile produced using default clip=1.2 — preliminary top-1 = 77.1% (delta -1.8%). INT8 preliminary = 78.5% (delta -0.4%).

2025-02-15 - Sasha Kim: Tuned FP8 clip/scale heuristics and re-ran with per-channel asymmetric clipping. New FP8 top-1 = 78.5% (delta -0.4%), p99 latency +9%. Results look promising but need second independent run for reproducibility.

2025-02-17 - Marco Ortega: Repro run completed with seed=20250212. FP8 confirmed at 78.5% (two runs within 0.1%). Collected full artifacts, logs, and evaluation notebook. Prepared draft customer report.
test_results_summary: FP8: top-1 78.5% (delta -0.4%), p99 token latency +9%, throughput -6%. INT8: top-1 78.6% (delta -0.3%), p99 latency +6%. Failure modes observed: specific rare tokens with distributional shift caused localized logits collapse under symmetric clipping; fixed by per-channel asymmetric clipping and small bias-correction during calibration.
notes: Decision rationale: prefer FP8 when unit-cost and latency targets matter; use tuned asymmetric per-channel FP8 profile to meet accuracy constraints. If any customer production traces show >1% drift post-rollout, revert immediately to INT8 and open an incident review.
Operations: coordinate canary window with customer during low-traffic hours (customer timezone CET mornings). On-call infra must approve namespace load prior to canary start.
Follow-ups: (a) upstream runtime improvement to export calibration histograms for faster tuning (ENG-12133), (b) add an automated drift detector to Console for custom quant profiles (PM-441)
